_comment: Hand-maintained inventory of what the build cannot learn from vcpkg.
vcpkg ports need no entry: their copyright files are read from the installed tree.
Qt modules come from qt-modules.json (generated by tools/licences/qt_sbom_manifest.py).
See docs/licensing.md for how this file, the generator and the test fit together.
elected: the option under which Qt's modules are distributed with this build.
Quick 3D is offered only as Commercial or GPL-3.0-only, so the whole Qt set is taken under GPL-3.0-only.
If Quick 3D ever leaves the app, Qt's LGPL-3.0-only option becomes available and this changes (docs/licensing.md).

fileAliases._comment: Only for libraries the Qt SBOMs do not list as packaged binaries; qt-modules.json 'files' is generated and covers every plugin and module library the SBOMs name.

repoNames.qtbase: Qt Base (Core, GUI, Network, Concurrent, platform plugins)
repoNames.qtdeclarative: Qt Declarative (QML, Qt Quick, Quick Controls 2, Labs Settings)

_comment: Qt components windeployqt puts beside the exe although the app names none of them directly.
Windows list: taken from the deployment scan of a real build on 2026-10-13 (Qt 6.8.3, RelWithDebInfo).
macOS, Linux and Android: fill in by running the notices test on a deployment of that platform (E4).
web: there is no deployment tool - Qt is linked into the one .wasm module - so nothing is deployed beside the app that its link line does not already name.
Qt modules that only test executables load. A test copies the module's shared library into the runtime
directory because that directory is shared by the app and the tests (CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY), so the
deployment scan sees a file that is evidence of the test, not of the app.
The deployment scan ignores a file that maps to a module listed here. Nothing else changes: if the app itself
links or imports one of these, the link line and QML imports still add it, with its whole licence closure.
An id that is not in qt-modules.json (renamed or dropped by a Qt upgrade) is reported as unresolved.
testOnlyModules.qtbase/Test: QtTest (Qt6Test.dll), copied next to cube_system_tests by tests/system/CMakeLists.txt: it sends the input events. The third-party code bundled in it (qtbase/Test_Attribution_*: Catch2, the FFTW cycle counter, Linux perf and valgrind headers) is reached only through it, so it is a notice duty only if Qt6Test ships.

licenseElections._comment: Where a component offers a choice of licences, the option taken. Keys are SPDX expressions as published.

textExemptions._comment: SPDX ids whose terms impose no notice or text-reproduction duty, so no text is bundled for them.
textExemptions.LicenseRef-Qt-Commercial: not a licence this build uses; the commercial option is not elected
textExemptions.blessing: SQLite's public-domain dedication (a blessing, not a licence with conditions); no text has to be reproduced

components.name: Lucide icon shapes (redrawn in Icon.qml)
components.notes: camera, globe, menu, sun and refresh. The copyright year is the one on Lucide's current LICENSE; the shapes were taken from an earlier release.

components.name: Feather icon shapes (via Lucide, redrawn in Icon.qml)
components.notes: chevron-left, chevron-right, check, alert-triangle and help-circle are on Lucide's list of icons derived from Feather.

ignoredFiles._comment: Files under assets/ and third_party/ that are not shipped works, so need no component.

portLicences._comment: vcpkg ports whose own manifest says license:null (or omits it). Each was read against the port's installed share/<port>/copyright.

_comment: Files the deployment tool puts beside the executable that are neither Qt's nor vcpkg's.
A name listed here is a known one: it is not reported. The value says what it is and what is decided.
A name NOT listed here is reported as a warning by the generator (it does not fail the build).
deployedFiles.clang_rt.asan_dynamic-x86_64.dll: AddressSanitizer runtime copied by cube_deploy_sanitizer_runtime into sanitizer builds only; never installed into a package.
